title: Anybody take a stab at duplicating Shadow of Wars nemesis system yet?
author: completelypositive
selftext: Keep reading about REA and co-op anything, and remaking games.. Has anyone taken a stab at rebuilding and porting the nemesis system?

comments.author: nayheyxus
comments.body:
The have a Patent for it, so I would not dare invoke the ire of Warner Bros

(US Patent No. 10,926,179).

replies.author: ziguslav
replies.body: They have a patent for that exact implementation. You can make your own though.

replies.author: caster
replies.body:
This is one of those situations where you are opening yourself up to a multi-million-dollar lawsuit. That is *probably* bullshit, but it will still ruin you even if you (probably) win.

There's just no upside to risking the kind of asshole fuckery you will be risking. Even if they are completely in the wrong and they know it.

replies.author: ziguslav
replies.body:
I'm really sorry, but you don't know what you're talking about.

Xcom 2 was able to do major parts of the nemesis system without getting sued.

You can make a nemesis-like system, it's not what's patented. What's patented is a very specific way it's implemented. I know this, because I've been doing gamedev for the last 10 years, and actually read the patent. You can read it yourself, here: [https://patents.google.com/patent/US20160279522A1/en](https://patents.google.com/patent/US20160279522A1/en)

You're parroting stupid journalism and just repeat "multi-million-dollar lawsuit" when in reality you'll get a C&D letter at worst before any kind of action follows.

Naturally I do think that patenting such things is stupid and shouldn't be allowed, but in reality the patent really isn't as prohibitively restrictive as people seem to think it is.

replies.author: completelypositive
replies.body: Duh? I wanted to know if anybody ELSE had built something like it already. Thanks for the mind-blowing insight, Sherlock.

replies.author: knowyourclass
replies.body:
Memory system for NPCs? Yes... procedurally generated behavior? Look into BDI system and make the Desires procedurally generated... it's really not that complicated

That patent got a lot of hype for no reason at all. But that's exactly why they patented it, for hype and marketing purposes. It's really nothing special AT ALL

replies.author: RamboJesus_
replies.body: Clearly you have no idea what you're talking about since you can't even describe it

replies.author: knowyourclass
replies.body: oh yeah? and what is it then...

replies.author: ziguslav
replies.body:
He literally described it. NPCs have basic memory, probably represented by a variable (I got **killed by** a *sword*, I **don't like** *Urshak*, *Tommy* **helped** me in the last **3 duels** against the *player*), and then these variables are used in procedurally generated behaviour. 

He even pointed you to the BDI pattern, which you're one search engine query away from finding out about.

comments.body: Be the change you want to see

comments.author: Dasmatarix
comments.body: It's not a complicated system to make, that is controversy over it. It's a simple system that in some people's opinions shouldn't have been granted a patent to protect it. Making it would be trivial, using it legally is not.

replies.body: Exatly. One characters influencing another's future actions is such a blatantly simple system its disgusting that they were able to patent it
